title: Senior's toolkit: shipping and rolling back
summary: Tags, release notes, environment approvals, canary promotion and idempotent migration scripts.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: shipping and rolling back
steps.body: A release is a tag, notes, a gated deploy and a tested way back. These are the commands behind each of those.

toolkit.what: The latest tag reachable from HEAD: the version you are about to bump.
flags: fall back to a short hash when there is no tag

toolkit.what: Everything that will ship in this release. Read it to choose major, minor or patch.
An annotated tag is the release marker; pushing it is what usually triggers the release workflow.
flags: annotated: has an author, date and message
push just this tag (`--tags` pushes every local tag)
toolkit.example: git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "Release 1.4.0" && git push origin v1.4.0

toolkit.what: Creates the GitHub release with notes built from the merged pull requests since the previous release.
flags: notes from PR titles, grouped by `.github/release.yml` labels
fail if the tag was not pushed yet

toolkit.what: Ties a job to a GitHub environment, so its protection rules apply: required reviewers, a wait timer, allowed branches, and its own secrets.
flags: a link shown on the run and the PR
toolkit.example:
jobs:
  deploy-prod:
    needs: deploy-staging
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://shop.example.com

toolkit.what: With Argo Rollouts, shows a canary's steps, traffic weight and analysis live. `promote` moves it to the next step, `abort` sends all traffic back to the stable version.
toolkit.example: kubectl argo rollouts promote api -n shop

toolkit.what: One SQL script that brings any older database version up to date and is safe to run twice. Review it and run it as its own pipeline step.
flags: checks the migrations history before each migration
write to a file you can review and keep as an artifact
only the migrations in a range

steps.prompt: Five minutes into a canary at 20% traffic, the error rate of the new pods is 4% against 0.2% on stable. Argo Rollouts manages the deployment. What do you run?
steps.explain: `abort` shifts all traffic back to the stable ReplicaSet at once. `promote` would push the bad version to more users. Good setups run an analysis that aborts automatically on this metric.

steps.prompt: Match the command to its place in a release.
pairs: see what is about to ship
require approval before the prod job runs

steps.prompt: Create a migration script that is safe to run against any older version of the database.
steps.explain: `--idempotent` wraps each migration in a check against `__EFMigrationsHistory`, so the same script works on staging (one behind) and production (two behind).

steps.prompt: Put a tagged release in order.
Rolling back the 1.4.0 app was fast, but the old version now throws `Invalid column name 'CustomerRef'`. The release renamed a column. What would have prevented this?
options: Expand and contract: add the new column first, ship code that works with both, and drop the old one in a later release
steps.explain: An app rollback does not roll back the schema. Changes that each version can live with (expand, migrate, contract) keep rollback safe.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Read `git log <last-tag>..HEAD` before you pick the version, release from a pushed tag, and put production behind an environment with reviewers. Know your rollback command (`rollout undo`, `argo rollouts abort`, a feature flag) before you ship, and keep schema changes backward compatible.
